seo.title: San Francisco Homeless Help - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified shelter, meals, hygiene, health care, benefits, jobs, legal help and other homelessness services in San Francisco.

content.text: Immediate danger, fire, overdose or medical emergency:
City information and non-emergency street outreach:
SF Homeless Outreach Team and adult shelter line:

notice.text: Information and capacity can change without notice.
Call ahead when possible. A listing does not guarantee a bed, meal, appointment, benefit, job, storage space or housing. Shelter and housing assessments are not promises of placement.

content.text: for immediate danger, serious injury, trouble breathing, unconsciousness, fire, suspected overdose or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location first. If naloxone is available during a suspected opioid overdose, use it and still call 911 because its effect can wear off.

Available 24 hours a day in more than 160 languages. Use 311 for non-emergency information, service referrals and a request for outreach to a person living outside. Use 911 when someone is in immediate danger.

items.name: SF Homeless Outreach Team and Adult Shelter Access Line

content.text: Request street outreach, ask about adult shelter access, or register for the adult shelter reservation waitlist. An outreach request or waitlist registration does not reserve a bed. For the waitlist, use either the phone or the online form, not both.
for suicide, mental-health or substance-use crisis support. For public behavioral-health assessment and treatment navigation, call
, select a language and extension 2. The access line operates 24 hours.
a shelter waitlist is for a temporary bed. Coordinated Entry assesses possible housing and problem-solving resources. Neither process guarantees placement.

For self-sufficient adults age 18 or older without minor children seeking a bed at Next Door, MSC South or Sanctuary. Register once by phone or through the official form. Keep the waitlist identifier and check the list regularly. Registration is not a same-day bed guarantee.

items.name: Dolores Shelter Program — walk-up overnight shelter

content.text: 1050 South Van Ness Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94110
overnight, 6 p.m.–8 a.m.; the first-come line may begin at 5:30 p.m.
Walk-up option for adults without minor children. Capacity is limited and lining up does not guarantee entry. Confirm the current intake process before making a long trip.
Adult shelter with meals, showers, case management and support. Access is through the adult shelter reservation system, 311 or SFHOT; it is not a guaranteed walk-in bed.
St. Vincent de Paul official program page

items.name: Adult Coordinated Entry — ECS Access Point

content.text: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 9 a.m.–noon and 12:30–3:45 p.m.; Wednesday, 9 a.m.–noon and 2–3:45 p.m.
For adults age 18 or older without minor children. Offers housing assessment and problem-solving. Assessment may not lead to a housing referral.
For adults age 18 or older without minor children. Ask for a housing assessment and problem-solving conversation. Bring documents if available, but call or visit even if papers are missing.
Housing access point for justice-involved adults age 18 or older without minor children. An assessment identifies possible next steps but does not guarantee housing.

items.name: Family Coordinated Entry — three access points

content.text: For households with a minor child and for pregnant people. Call first to confirm hours:
Access points provide problem-solving, assessment and navigation. They do not guarantee immediate shelter or permanent housing.
SFUSD family and youth housing resources
Call before traveling. Eligibility, intake and spaces change, and a call does not reserve a room.
. Open 24 hours; walk-ins are listed as available.
Nightly bed availability is limited. Young people should arrive by 9:45 p.m. The shelter provides meals, showers, laundry, lockers and a pet kennel. A listing does not guarantee a bed.
Shelter and services for transgender, gender-nonconforming and intersex people, and cisgender women. The site is not open to public walk-ins and its address is not published.
For assessment and referral, go to Adult Coordinated Entry at 123 10th Street. Referral and capacity are not guaranteed.

items.name: Urgent accommodation for survivors of violence

content.text: Ask about short-term urgent accommodation for an adult fleeing intimate-partner violence, sexual assault or human trafficking while homeless. Eligibility and room availability must be confirmed.

items.name: Veterans Coordinated Entry — Swords to Plowshares

content.text: Monday, 9 a.m.–3:45 p.m.; Tuesday–Friday, 8 a.m.–3:45 p.m.
For veterans age 18 or older without minor children. Staff can assess housing needs and help obtain service documents. Off-site housing does not accept direct walk-ins.

categories.title: 3. Free meals, groceries and faith-based help

content.text: breakfast daily 7:30–9 a.m.; lunch 11:30 a.m.–1 p.m.; dinner 3:30–5 p.m. The first half-hour of breakfast is reserved for seniors, families and adults with disabilities.
No eligibility screening or intake is required. GLIDE is rooted in a church community; worship is not listed as a meal requirement.
121 Golden Gate Avenue, first floor, San Francisco, CA 94102
breakfast begins at 7 a.m.; lunch is 10 a.m.–1:30 p.m.; a weekday hot meal to go begins at 2 p.m.
Franciscan Catholic organization serving the public. Worship is not listed as a requirement.

items.name: Martin de Porres House of Hospitality

content.text: Volunteer-run Catholic Worker community. All are welcome and help is offered without conditions. Meals are often vegetarian and frequently vegan.

items.name: Bayview Drop-In Center and Mother Brown's Kitchen

content.text: No proof of income or outside referral is required, but a general program intake is used. Meals are to go.

items.name: San Francisco-Marin Food Bank pantry locator

content.text: Use the live locator or call 211 to find free weekly groceries, emergency food and older-adult food boxes. The Food Bank does not distribute directly to the public at its warehouses.
Sites have different registration and pickup rules. Call before traveling and bring bags if possible.
The Human Services Agency publishes meal and grocery partners across the city and advises calling each site to confirm hours and availability.

categories.title: 4. Showers, laundry, clothing, toilets, mail and internet

content.text: 150 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94102
Free showers, toilets, laundry, hygiene supplies and basic-needs help. Sign-up begins at 6 a.m. and demand can exceed daily capacity. Check the official page or call
. Showers and laundry are published daily 8 a.m.–midnight, with last shower at 11:30 p.m. and last wash at 11 p.m. Lockers, rest space and weekday mail service are also available.
A general intake is required. Cleaning closures and availability can affect access.
. Drop-in space, showers, laundry, lockers, restrooms, charging, case management and a clinic. Service windows and women-only periods vary; call before traveling.

items.name: Martin de Porres showers and clothing

content.text: 121 Golden Gate Avenue, second floor, San Francisco, CA 94102

Adults and families with self-determined need may use the program, but an appointment is required. New or returning-after-one-year guests register in person on the first floor. No appointments are made by phone or email.
150 Golden Gate Avenue, third floor, San Francisco, CA 94102
. Free computers, internet, printing, scanning, faxing, secure charging, classes and tutoring for adults 18 or older.
No ID is required, but a short annual orientation is. Check the program page for current hours.
. Libraries provide indoor public space, restrooms, internet and computer access under library rules. Check the live directory for hours, closures and a closer branch.
The City publishes a live map of public bathrooms and water fountains. Hours, closures and accessibility vary by location.

items.name: Project Homeless Connect — mail and practical support

content.text: 1031 Franklin Street, second floor, entrance at Franklin and O'Farrell, San Francisco, CA 94109
Tuesday, 9:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m.; check the calendar for more days.
Offers mail service, referrals, identification help, some health connections and donated items. Appointments, eligibility and stock vary.

items.name: Sixth Street Storage and other lockers

content.text: The City-funded program remains contracted through 2029, but enrollment, hours and available bins can change. Call 311 or ask an access point before taking belongings there. Bayview Drop-In and Mission Neighborhood Resource Center also list lockers, subject to intake and capacity.

categories.title: 5. Medical, mental health and substance-use care

content.text: 230 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94102
. Focuses on adults experiencing homelessness, supportive-housing residents and Tenderloin residents; walk-ins are welcome.
Monday–Wednesday and Friday, 8 a.m.–noon and 1–5 p.m.; Thursday, 1–5 p.m.; closed weekends and City holidays.
Free urgent and preventive care for unhoused San Franciscans, with connections to primary care. The schedule includes roving sites and can change. Call for the exact location.

City shelter guests can ask staff for on-site health care, including urgent and wound care, vaccines, medication support, testing and connections to mental-health or substance-use care. This program serves guests at participating shelters; it is not a public walk-in clinic.
1380 Howard Street, first floor, San Francisco, CA 94103
weekdays 8 a.m.–7 p.m.; weekends 9 a.m.–4 p.m.
Mental-health assessment and referral for San Francisco residents eligible for Medi-Cal. For 24-hour navigation, call
. Drop-in mental-health stabilization and short-term counseling. The City guide lists Monday 2–10 p.m. and Tuesday–Friday 9 a.m.–10 p.m.

Safer-use supplies, naloxone, syringe disposal, overdose-prevention support, drug checking on selected days, testing and links to care. The latest City schedule found lists Tuesday–Friday 11 a.m.–7 p.m.; confirm before traveling.
Call 911 for a suspected overdose, even after giving naloxone.
. Apply online, by phone or at an SFHSA center. A person experiencing homelessness does not need a household address to start.
If income and money are very low, ask for
, which may provide eligible applicants benefits within three business days. People without stable mail or phone may ask about EBT-card pickup.
. Apply through BenefitsCal or in person at 1460 Mission Street.
County cash-assistance programs for eligible low-income adults without dependent children. Ask about shelter connected to the application process; neither cash aid nor shelter is automatic.
. Apply online or visit 170 Otis Street or 3120 Mission Street.
Tell the worker immediately if the family urgently needs housing, food, clothing, rent, utilities or medical help; emergency help depends on eligibility.
. Apply through BenefitsCal, by phone or at an SFHSA center. Low-income California residents may qualify regardless of age or immigration status, but eligibility review is required.

items.name: SFHSA service centers and mobile service

content.text: In-person benefits help is available at 1460 Mission Street, 1440 Harrison Street, 3120 Mission Street, 170 Otis Street and 2 Gough Street for older adults and people with disabilities. Confirm hours before traveling.
1235 Mission Street is permanently closed. The Mobile Benefits Center calendar offers additional temporary locations and can issue EBT cards when appropriate.

A 12-month Muni-only pass for eligible people experiencing homelessness in San Francisco. Applicants must have contacted a Coordinated Entry Access Point within the previous six months. It does not cover BART.
Apply online, by mail, or at the SFMTA Customer Service Center, 11 South Van Ness Avenue, weekdays 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
Official SFMTA discounts and Access Pass

items.name: Centralized Job Center of San Francisco

content.text: Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., walk-in or appointment; orientations Tuesday and Thursday at 11 a.m.
Free Goodwill career services may include planning, training, hiring events, job boards, and use of computers, phones and fax. Enrollment requirements vary by program.

items.name: Specialized Job Center for justice-involved adults

content.text: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m., walk-in or appointment.
Career services and training within the Community Assessment and Services Center for people facing re-entry barriers.

Free SFHSA job matching, paid opportunities, training, résumé, application and interview help. Eligibility generally requires authorization to work and current SFHSA benefits such as CalWORKs, CalFresh or CAAP.
Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Benefits service center with JobsNOW! connections plus computers, printing, copying and fax for job search.

items.name: Larkin Street employment and education — ages 18–24

content.text: 134 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94102
. Youth support includes employment, education, GED, college, computers and case management. Walk-in navigation is Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–noon; appointments 1–4 p.m.

Use an authorized mail program rather than an address that has not agreed to receive mail. Project Homeless Connect offers mail service, and Bayview Drop-In lists weekday mail service. The St. Anthony Tech Lab provides free computers, printing, scanning, fax and charging.
Never pay someone who promises a job or asks for money for an application.
1031 Franklin Street, second floor, San Francisco, CA 94109
. Eligible participants may receive a no-fee California ID voucher and help seeking birth certificates or passports. Help depends on eligibility, appointments and funds.

A person experiencing homelessness may request a certified California birth record without the normal fee. A qualifying homeless-services provider must complete the affidavit; identity and record requirements still apply.
California Vital Records and fee-waiver forms

Free legal and social-service help for people experiencing or at imminent risk of homelessness, including disability benefits, eviction, SSI and immigration documentation. New-client drop-in is Tuesday–Friday, 1–3 p.m.; closed Mondays.

items.name: Legal Advice and Referral Clinic at GLIDE

content.text: GLIDE Sanctuary, second floor, 330 Ellis Street, San Francisco, CA 94102
third Wednesday monthly, 10 a.m.–noon, walk-in. Low-income people receive priority. Volunteer lawyers provide brief civil advice and referrals; representation is not guaranteed.
The City lists nonprofit legal providers by language and type of case. Call before visiting; eligibility and case capacity differ. Do not pay a notario or unlicensed adviser for legal representation.
Official San Francisco immigration legal resources

categories.title: 9. Families, young people, survivors, LGBTQ+ people and veterans

content.text: Call 911 for immediate danger. For confidential support, call
Confidential shelter addresses are not published. If an abusive person may monitor the device, use a safe telephone if possible.
. St. Vincent de Paul provides confidential survivor support, emergency shelter, transitional housing, case management and advocacy.
Brennan House accepts all genders, including male survivors, and children. Availability requires assessment.

Drop-in help for women experiencing homelessness and sexual exploitation: food, bathrooms, hygiene, computers and connections to housing, legal and health services. It is not a guaranteed overnight bed.
134 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94102
. Drop-in support includes breakfast, lunch, showers, laundry, rest pods, computers, Wi-Fi, clinic care, counseling, education and employment.
The Center serves LGBTQ+ young people with drop-in support and acts as a Youth Coordinated Entry access point. Ask about current housing navigation, employment and community services.
. No-fee case management, benefits and discharge assistance, legal help, employment, counseling and housing navigation. Staff can help obtain ID and DD-214 records.
Drop-ins are accepted for services, but off-site housing is referral-only.
. Walk-in medical and social-work services Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

items.name: Help in other languages and for immigrants

content.text: 311 provides free language assistance. SFHSA lists benefit-application partners serving Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin and other language communities. Immigration status affects some benefits but not every service; ask a qualified worker.

Tell every shelter or access point about an animal before accepting placement. A pet, service animal and emotional-support animal may be treated differently. Do not surrender an animal before asking about a kennel, temporary care, food or veterinary support.

items.name: Veterinary Street Outreach Services — Vet SOS

content.text: . Free twice-monthly pop-up veterinary clinics for unhoused San Francisco pet owners and some recently housed clients.
Wellness exams, vaccines, testing, supplies and referrals for free spay or neuter care. Appointment and eligibility confirmation are required; this is not emergency care.
. Free pet food, veterinary wellness help, grooming and supplies to unhoused people with dogs and cats through mobile events.
The Food 4 Paws page lists recurring distributions. Dates change; call or check before traveling.
Affordable preventive care and treatment for selected minor conditions. It does not provide emergencies, X-rays, laboratory diagnostics, adoption or health certificates.
Lark-Inn publishes a pet kennel for youth ages 18–24. Other shelter rules differ. When calling
or an access point, state the animal type, size and whether it is a trained service animal.
A kennel or animal-friendly policy does not guarantee a human shelter bed or space for the animal.
